summary: Updates BCP 101 to tell the IETF Administrative Oversight Committee to set more practical start and end dates for member terms, since the original dates were found impractical. It was replaced by RFC 8711.

eli5.summary: The rules for when committee terms begin and end were awkward, so they got changed. It was replaced by RFC 8711.

questions: when do iaoc terms start and end
what changed in bcp 101 about iaoc terms
subtitle: Practical fixes for when IETF committee members' terms should begin and end

tldr.problem: BCP 101 said the IAOC's (IETF Administrative Oversight Committee) member terms should end at the first IETF meeting of each year, but this schedule made it impossible for the committee to conduct business or elect a new chair during that meeting week.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 7691 updates BCP 101 to let the IAOC decide when its terms start and end, as long as the transition happens near the annual meeting. The IAOC elects its chair at that meeting before the transition takes effect.
tldr.outcome: The committee can now function smoothly during the week of leadership transitions. RFC 7691 was superseded by RFC 8711.

today: RFC 7691 is Historic. It was superseded by RFC 8711, which provides further updates to the IAOC governance structure.

sections.title: The Problem: Terms Ending at the Wrong Time
sections.content:
RFC 4071 (BCP 101) said IAOC member terms must end at the end of the first IETF meeting of the year. But this created chaos: the IAOC needs to hold meetings during that week, and it must elect a new chair. If the new members aren't yet seated, no one knows who should vote, who can be elected chair, or whether the committee can reach a quorum.

For years the IAOC worked around this by letting the transition happen during the administrative plenary after the face-to-face meeting, but this violated BCP 101 and still created confusion.
sections.eli5: The committee had to swap out its leaders at a big meeting, but the timing meant new leaders couldn't sit down until after all the votes. It was confusing and nobody was sure who was in charge.

sections.title: New Flexibility for Term Dates
sections.content:
RFC 7691 removes the rigid requirement and instead directs the IAOC to hold a regular meeting near or during the first IETF meeting of the year. The IAOC itself decides the beginning and end dates of its members' terms, as long as those dates cluster around this annual meeting. The committee elects its chair as its first order of business in its own meeting, before the transition occurs.

This lets the committee schedule the transition in a way that actually works, and ensures the new chair-elect knows their team before the IETF meeting opens.
sections.eli5: Now the committee can pick its own timing, as long as transitions happen near the big meeting. It picks a new chair first, with everybody knowing who the team is.

sections.title: Why This Matters
sections.content:
The IAOC members serve as Trustees of the IETF Trust, which manages intellectual property and other assets. The same timing problems affected the Trust, so the same fix applies. The update also clarifies that a regular meeting can be held face-to-face, by teleconference, or as a hybrid.

This change was a practical necessity: smooth transitions require clear procedures, not deadlock and improvisation.
sections.eli5: The committee's leaders also manage important funds and documents, so when they change, things need to work smoothly. This lets them transition properly without everyone confused about who is in charge.
